summary: Scoped review of the proposed Range MCP boundary and changed rules, not a certification of the entire legacy ruleset. New identity has no direct catalogue/stock/supplier/approval/storage authority; strict server validation and exact human approval protect Admin SDK writes. Prototype only, not deployed.

findings.issue: Existing Range recursive child wildcard also matched parent writes in rules v2, bypassing new family reservation validation. Fixed by requiring a subcollection/document path; emulator rejection tests cover unreserved parent writes.
findings.recommendation: Retain the regression and require this rules change with the release.

findings.issue: Server Admin SDK bypasses client rules by design. New UID/profile/control and exact owner approval are checked inside transactions; no raw write tool is exposed. Direct service access remains denied even if misprofiled.
findings.recommendation: Review endpoint and private provisioning separately; never grant ordinary modules or share server credentials with MCP clients.

findings.issue: Old cached normal forms and external privileged scripts do not participate in the new claims contract. Normal create/code-change paths in this branch are migrated; old client creates fail closed after rules release.
findings.recommendation: Use coordinated maintenance cutover, reload clients, and pause/migrate privileged external writers before enabling the generic capability.

findings.issue: Server performs bounded legacy scans (2000 families/components) and conservative transaction revalidation. This is safe but will not scale indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Keep rate/request/output limits and fail closed at the cap; review an indexed migration before raising it.

findings.issue: Current approved-customer rules allow hidden family reads by ID. Supplier costs and unrelated private data are redacted by MCP readback and are not written onto the family.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat active:false as confidentiality; retain private supplier/quote collections.
